# Adversarial review of the three tool concept documents, round 1

Run 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-20. Decision entry: DECISIONS.md D28.

Structure: five independent audit agents (one citation audit per document, one
measurement-reproduction agent, one cross-document consistency agent on a
different model family than the documents' writers), refute-by-default
verification of every surviving high or medium finding by a further independent
agent per finding. 15 agents total, 434 claims checked. No agent wrote to the
repository.

Findings below are recorded verbatim from the workflow's returned data, not
retyped. Corrections for the confirmed findings were applied to the concept
documents on 2026-08-20 and are marked `[CORRECTED 2026-08-20]` in place.

Scoreboard: 31 deduped findings; 10 verified adversarially; **8 confirmed, 2
refuted by the verifier**; 21 reported unverified below (4 medium, 17 low).
The two refuted findings are kept here because they are the evidence the
verification layer earns its cost: both looked plausible and both were wrong.

---

## Confirmed findings (verified by independent refutation attempt)

### C1. [high, verdict-impacting] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, A.2

**Doc's claim:** "18 U.S.C. 3161(h), excludable time | 0" pages mention it, and therefore "Seven of the eleven rows are zero"; A.5 and B.3 repeat that (h) is text "no page carries".

**Finding:** pageCopy over the written federal and white-collar pages shows 3161(h) on SIX pages: /federal-criminal-defense/wire-mail-fraud, /conspiracy-charges, /weapons-gun-offenses, /money-laundering, /computer-internet-crimes, and /white-collar-defense/bank-fraud. The treatment is substantive, not passing: src/lib/site.ts line 4186 ("18 U.S.C. 3161(h) lists periods of delay that are excluded from both computations above..."), line 5128, lines 5269-5271 (quoting (h)(1), (h)(1)(D) and (h)(6) at length on the conspiracy page), line 5888, and lines 6072 and 6318. Only five of the eleven table rows are actually zero (Rule 5.1, Rule 11, Rule 32, 3553(a), and Rule 5 as a citation).

**Verifier:** The finding is confirmed, not refuted. GUIDES-CONCEPT.md A.2 (line 131) claims 0 pages mention 18 U.S.C. 3161(h) and concludes "Seven of the eleven rows are zero" (line 135), repeated at A.5 (line 243) and B.3 (line 451) as text "no page carries." But src/lib/site.ts contains 8 substantive occurrences of 3161(h) across exactly the six pages the finding names: federal/money-laundering (line 4186), federal/computer-internet-crimes (5128), federal/conspiracy-charges (5269-5271, quoting (h)(1), (h)(1)(D), and (h)(6) at length), federal/weapons-gun-offenses (5888), federal/wire-mail-fraud (6072), and white-collar/bank-fraud (6318). Timing offers no excuse: the 3161(h) copy landed in commits on 2026-08-14 (first a1764bf) and is present at HEAD, while the doc's file was created 2026-08-19, so the claim was false when written. The finding's secondary arithmetic also holds: 3161(c)(2) appears once (line 4185, federal/money-laundering), so that "0" row is wrong too, and only Rule 5.1, Rule 11, Rule 32, and 3553(a) are genuinely absent. Severity high is appropriate since the "build guide 2" verdict rests on the vacancy claim.

### C2. [high, verdict-impacting] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, A.2

**Doc's claim:** "18 U.S.C. 3161(c)(2), the 30-day minimum before trial may begin | 0" pages; C.2 repeats "Absent from the site" and A.5 assigns it to guide 2 as text no page carries.

**Finding:** src/lib/site.ts line 4185, rendered on /federal-criminal-defense/money-laundering (confirmed via pageCopy): "18 U.S.C. 3161(c)(2) provides that unless the defendant consents in writing to the contrary, trial must not commence less than thirty days from the date on which the defendant first appears through counsel or expressly waives counsel and elects to proceed pro se. It is a floor on how fast a case can be brought to trial, not a schedule for it." That is a full statement of the provision on a published-track charge page, so a guide quoting (c)(2) shares text with an existing page, contrary to B.3's premise that "runs built on text no page carries cannot be shared runs".

**Verifier:** The finding is confirmed, not refuted. GUIDES-CONCEPT.md (written 2026-08-19, self-declared as measured over pageCopy against the working tree that day and "reproducible from the current tree") claims at A.2 line 132 that 18 U.S.C. 3161(c)(2) appears on 0 pages, at C.2 line 450 that it is "Absent from the site," and at A.5 line 243 that no page carries (c)(2) or (h). But src/lib/site.ts (last modified 2026-08-14, before the doc) line 4185, inside CHARGE_CONTENT["federal/money-laundering"], carries a full statement of (c)(2), and line 4186 a full (h) treatment. pageCopy (page-copy.ts line 104) extracts these steps[].when|what fields; re-running the doc's probe over pageCopy for all written charge pages yields (c)(2) on 1 page and (h) on 6 pages (doc claims 0 for both), and 3161 on 12 pages (doc says 11). The page renders at /federal-criminal-defense/money-laundering via the federal [charge] route and ChargeTemplate (steps rendered at lines 410-417). So B.3's lever-1 premise fails for these provisions exactly as alleged: a guide quoting (c)(2)/(h) can share eight-word runs with an existing page. The finding's only flaw is calling it a "published-track" page: every charge page is published: false (noindex, out of sitemap) on this pre-launch site. That is immaterial because the doc's own corpus was written charge pages probed via pageCopy, which this page is in. Severity stays high: A.2's "seven of the eleven rows are zero" is actually five of eleven, and the dedup strategy in B.3 that the build verdict relies on assigns guide 2 provisions that are not in fact unshared.

### C3. [high, verdict-impacting] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, A.1

**Doc's claim:** "Every one of them [all eleven state charge pages] already states" the full listed set: Rule 3.111(a) earliest-of-three plus 3.111(b)(1)'s no-incarceration limiter, the booking officer's duties under 3.111(c)(1)-(3), the right to decline to answer questions, the Public Defender, 60-and-63-day and 90-and-175-day figures, the (e) and (f) limitations, and the capias start-date clause.

**Finding:** Probing pageCopy for each state page: Rule 3.111 appears NOWHERE on /criminal-defense/drug-trafficking-defense, /grand-theft-defense, or /dui-defense (no 3.111, no earliest-of-three, no no-incarceration limiter). The booking-officer duties (3.111(c)) appear on only 4 of 11 pages (sexual-battery, gun-crimes, battery, computer-crimes); "booking officer" occurs 5 times in all of src/lib/site.ts. The Public Defender is absent from 4 pages (drug-trafficking, drug-possession, domestic-violence, dui). Decline-to-answer/remain-silent language is absent from domestic-violence and dui. The 63-day figure is absent from domestic-violence; the 90-day misdemeanor period is absent from drug-trafficking; the capias clause is absent from dui; the Rule 3.191(a) (e)/(f) limitations are named on only 4 of 11 pages (drug-possession, sex-crimes, domestic-violence, homicide). The 3.130(a) carve-out, 3.134 with the "unless the state files" condition, 175 days, the (o) remedy, and the SAO/courthouse facts do appear on all 11, so the overlap is real but materially narrower than "no sentence to say that is not already on those pages" (Section 0's guide-1 basis).

**Verifier:** Reproduced the finding's probe by extracting pageCopy (src/lib/page-copy.ts) for all 11 written state charge pages in src/lib/site.ts. The doc's A.1 universal claim fails on multiple pages: Rule 3.111 (a), (b)(1), and earliest-of-three appear nowhere on drug-trafficking-defense, grand-theft-defense, or dui-defense (those pages ground counsel in Rule 3.130(b)/(c) instead); 3.111(c) booking-officer duties appear on exactly the 4 pages the finding names; the Public Defender is absent from exactly the 4 pages named (zero occurrences of "defender"); the 63-day figure is absent from domestic-violence; the 90-day misdemeanor period is absent from drug-trafficking; capias is absent from dui; and the 3.191 (e)/(f) limitations are named on exactly the 4 pages the finding lists. The finding's concessions (3.130(a), 3.134 with the unless-the-state-files condition, 175 days, (o) remedy on all 11) also verified. One sub-claim in the finding is wrong: domestic-violence DOES carry decline-to-answer language ("Declining to answer questions is a right..."), only dui lacks it; this single error does not restore the doc's claim, since domestic-violence still misses the Public Defender, 63-day figure, and 3.111(c) duties. ChargeTemplate.tsx adds no shared boilerplate that could supply the missing facts. The finding survives; severity high is appropriate because Section 0's verdict against guide 1 rests on the falsified "no sentence to say that is not already on those pages" basis.

### C4. [high] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, 0, 'The measurement that decides it' (lines 72-75), restated in B

**Doc's claim:** "Ten existing page pairs are already at or above the 5% limit when only one side's procedure sections are measured."

**Finding:** Reimplemented check-pages.mts shingles/compelled/min-denominator exactly (scripts/check-pages.mts lines 761-840) and measured procedure-sections (ids timeline/clocks/now/who, the set that reproduces the doc's own three procedure rows to the digit: 11.37%/94, 7.75%/94, 5.58%/113) of each page against every other whole page. Result: 24 undirected page pairs (31 directed comparisons) are at or above 5%, not ten. No tested variant yields ten: adding 'forum' gives 22 undirected, kind-based timeline+guidance gives 18, state-silo-only gives 9, both-directions-over-5% gives 6. The doc's header (lines 19-23) claims every number is reproducible from the current tree; this one is not. The error understates the overlap, so it strengthens rather than weakens the doc's do-not-isolate-procedure argument.

**Verifier:** Independently reimplemented check-pages.mts's duplication measure (shingles, compelled-set from COMPELLED_PHRASES + STATUTES quotes/triggers + PAGE-SOURCES.md blockquotes, min non-compelled denominator) over the real charges/pageCopy data. The reimplementation reproduces every reproducible number in GUIDES-CONCEPT.md Section 0 to the digit (11.37%/94, 7.75%/94, 5.58%/113 for the three procedure rows with ids timeline/clocks/now/who, and 4.73%/221 for the worst whole-vs-whole pair), confirming the methodology is the doc's own. Under that methodology, page pairs at or above the 5% limit when one side's procedure sections are measured against the other's whole page number 31 directed / 24 undirected, exactly as the finding claims, not ten. Swept alternative readings (proc-side state only: 12/9; both-state: 9/6; kind-based timeline+guidance: 23/18; timeline kind only: 46/33; ids+forum: 28/22; proc-vs-proc: 22/11); no defensible reading yields ten, and the sole coincidental 10 (kind-based, both-state, directed) contradicts the doc's own example rows and its unrestricted phrasing. The doc's claim is not reproducible from the tree despite its header guarantee, so the finding stands. Severity corrected to medium: the error understates the overlap by ~2.4x and therefore strengthens the doc's do-not-isolate-procedure conclusion; it affects no verdict or recommendation, though it does breach the doc's every-number-reproducible promise.

### C5. [medium] SEAL-EXPUNGE-CONCEPT.md, F.2, hostile fact pattern 6

**Doc's claim:** "'Misdemeanor battery, my ex-wife.' (2)(f): a second degree misdemeanor is permanently disqualifying because of the relationship, not the degree."

**Finding:** The audited row the pattern must trace to, src/lib/statute-tables/fs-943-0584.ts line 27 (943.0584(2)(f)), assigns "second degree misdemeanor" only to simple assault: "simple assault (s. 784.011, a second degree misdemeanor in its own statute) and simple battery (s. 784.03)". The repo's own recorded copy at src/lib/site.ts line 1827 quotes F.S. 784.03(1)(b): battery "commits a misdemeanor of the first degree." So for the battery fact pattern the stated correct answer carries the wrong degree; nothing in the repository supports battery as a second degree misdemeanor. The relationship-not-degree point survives, but the answer key sentence is wrong as written, in a section whose own rule is that correct answers are traced to a row or a recorded fetch.

**Verifier:** The finding survives. SEAL-EXPUNGE-CONCEPT.md lines 727-728 (F.2 pattern 6) pose "Misdemeanor battery, my ex-wife" and label it "a second degree misdemeanor." The audited row it must trace to, src/lib/statute-tables/fs-943-0584.ts line 27 (943.0584(2)(f)), assigns second degree misdemeanor only to simple assault under s. 784.011 and gives no degree for battery. The repo's audited battery table, src/lib/statute-tables/fs-784-03.ts line 21 (784.03(1)(b)), records battery as a first degree misdemeanor with the verbatim statutory quote "commits a misdemeanor of the first degree," and src/lib/site.ts line 1827 quotes the same text. No repo source supports battery as a second degree misdemeanor, so the answer key sentence carries the wrong degree for the stated fact pattern, violating F.2's own traceability rule. The finding accurately characterizes both the doc and the sources; the relationship-not-degree substance of the pattern is unaffected, consistent with the finding's non-verdict-impacting framing.

### C6. [medium] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, C.2

**Doc's claim:** 18 U.S.C. 3161(h) is in the "Not recorded. New fact-layer work" table, i.e. no record of it exists in PAGE-SOURCES.md.

**Finding:** docs/research/PAGE-SOURCES.md lines 1418-1421 (white-collar/bank-fraud batch B record) record "18 U.S.C. 3161(b), (c)(1), (h)" with (h)'s opening clause quoted verbatim inside a blockquote line plus (h)(1)(D) in full, so that text is already in the compelled exclusion set. The record is not whole-section ("paragraphs not reproduced here"), so a read-whole fetch is still needed, but the binary "not recorded" is wrong and G.2's ranking rests on it.

**Verifier:** The finding survives. PAGE-SOURCES.md lines 1418-1421 (batch B repair round 1, white-collar/bank-fraud, recorded 2026-08-14) do record 18 U.S.C. 3161(h): the blockquote quotes (h)'s opening clause verbatim and (h)(1)(D) in full, marked as partial ("paragraphs not reproduced here"). Because scripts/check-pages.mts builds the compelled exclusion set from every blockquote line in PAGE-SOURCES.md (regex ^\s\*>\s? at lines ~817-825), that (h) text is already in the exclusion set, exactly as the finding says. GUIDES-CONCEPT.md C.2 (line 451) nonetheless places 3161(h) in the table headed "Not recorded. New fact-layer work", and the doc nowhere cites lines 1418-1421 or the batch B record at all -- its "Recorded" table cites only the older records at 1185-1187 and 970-976 for (b) and (c)(1), even though the batch B record duplicates both. So the binary "not recorded" is factually wrong and reflects a missed record, not deliberate precision about a whole-section read. I could not refute the core claim. Two mitigations lower the severity: (a) the doc's prescribed action is unchanged, since a read-whole fetch of (h) is still required (the finding concedes this), and (b) the finding's assertion that "G.2's ranking rests on it" is overstated -- G.2 item 2 (doc line 923) ranks (h) as the worst truncation risk on substantive grounds (a "70 days" sentence without excludable time misleads readers), which holds regardless of record status. The error is a record-indexing inaccuracy with no change to the work plan, so low rather than medium.

### C8. [medium] GUIDES-CONCEPT.md, 0, measurement table row 5 (line 70)

**Doc's claim:** "A guide assembled from every state page's procedure sections, against computer-crimes: 39.8% / 1,796 runs"

**Finding:** With the same procedure-section definition that reproduces the doc's other three procedure rows exactly (ids timeline/clocks/now/who), the assembly of all 11 state pages vs /criminal-defense/computer-crimes-defense measures 33.44% / 1,509 runs (guide non-compelled 12,277; computer-crimes 4,512, the smaller denominator; note 1,796/4,512 = 39.81%, so the doc used the same denominator). Adding 'forum' gives 41.51% / 1,873; a brute-force search over 512 procedural-id subsets plus per-page/per-section shingle unions and heading-exclusion variants never produced 1,796 (closest 1,814 at 40.20%). Against the federal computer-internet-crimes page it is 0.21%. The number is not reproducible as stated; the qualitative point (far above 5%) holds under every variant.

**Verifier:** Independent reimplementation of check-pages.mts's duplication measure (shingle function, compelled set from COMPELLED_PHRASES + STATUTES quote/trigger fields + PAGE-SOURCES.md blockquotes, pageCopy extraction) reproduces the doc's other measurement rows exactly: compelled set 124,381 runs; worst pair 4.73%/221 (wire-mail-fraud x money-laundering); procedure rows 11.37%/94, 7.75%/94, 5.58%/113 with ids timeline/clocks/now/who. With that same verified-faithful definition, the row-5 assembly of all 11 state pages' procedure sections vs /criminal-defense/computer-crimes-defense measures 33.44%/1,509 (guide non-compelled 12,277; computer-crimes 4,512), matching the finding, not the doc's 39.8%/1,796. Adding 'forum' gives 41.51%/1,873, also as the finding states. A search wider than the auditor's (65,536 procedural-id subsets, with/without computer-crimes' own sections, kind-based selections, per-page/per-section unions vs concatenation, whole-page assemblies, and cc-procedure-only comparisons) never yields 1,796 shared runs; closest is 1,873. The doc's rate/runs pair is internally consistent only in that 1,796/4,512 = 39.80%, confirming the denominator but not the shared count. The finding accurately characterizes both the doc and the source; the number is not reproducible as stated, though the qualitative conclusion (far above the 5% limit) holds under every variant, so medium severity and non-verdict-impacting are correct.

## Findings refuted by the verifier (the audit was wrong, the doc was right)

### SENTENCING-BOND-CONCEPT.md (vs GUIDES-CONCEPT.md)

**Alleged:** SENTENCING issues a final verdict: 'DO NOT BUILD the bond estimator. Publish the schedule as a reference section inside /resources/guides/after-an-arrest' and in B.4 directs 'delete the row from tools rather than leaving a published: false entry.' GUIDES, written the same day, says the same estimator-vs-guide collision 'has to be decided by a person before anything is written' (Phase 3: 'Not shippable. Blocking.'), and that if the person decides the estimator keeps the ground, 'guide 1 has no subject left and the correct outcome is to remove it from tools.'

**Why refuted:** The finding mischaracterizes both documents, and its central claim that "the two docs cannot both be followed" fails on the sources.

1. SENTENCING does not treat the build/kill decision as closed or preempt a human decision. The doc self-describes as "concept and recommendation" ("Concept document only. No code was written"), Section 0 is titled "The recommendations in one place," and B.2 opens the disposition with the word "Recommendation: DO NOT BUILD...". B.2 then explicitly contemplates the human decision going the other way: "If the client insists on a bond tool anyway, the only version that survives is a schedule reader..." A document that argues a recommendation and provides the fallback if the client overrules it is an input to exactly the person-decides step GUIDES Phase 3 requires, not a substitute for it. The finding's word "unconditionally" is contradicted by B.2's own client-override clause and by SENTENCING OQ6, which questions whether the bond section belongs in /resources/guides/after-an-arrest at all before 2026-12-31.

2. The finding's claim that "SENTENCING's only open question on the asset is row mechanics (OQ9), not build/kill" is factually wrong: OQ6 is a second open question on the same asset (whether the guide placement itself is right), and B.2's "if the client insists" clause shows build/kill is understood as the client's call. A.6's whole structure ("What would change my mind, in both directions") shows the doc's verdicts are argued positions awaiting review, not executed decisions.

3. The substantive recommendations of the two docs AGREE rather than collide. GUIDES OQ1's own recommendation is "the guide absorbs it, and the estimator entry is either removed or narrowed to a cost widget inside the guide." SENTENCING B.2 recommends exactly that: kill the estimator, put the schedule in the after-an-arrest guide, and keep only "the cash versus surety cost comparison" (the cost widget) as the surviving interactive element. Two same-day concept docs converging on the same answer, one of them adding that the decision must be recorded by a person in DECISIONS.md, is concurrence plus a process requirement, not a contradiction.

4. The alleged deletion conflict (SENTENCING B.4 "delete the row" vs GUIDES D.1 "delete nothing from tools in the same commit that adds guides") compares a conditional disposition with a commit-hygiene rule. B.4 is expressly conditional ("If the bond estimator is not built, delete the row from tools rather than leaving a published: false entry") and SENTENCING itself restates the delete-vs-dormant choice as OPEN in OQ9, so B.4 does not "direct delete... now" as the finding asserts. GUIDES D.1 only forbids deleting in the same commit that adds the guides array (to avoid D13-shape drift); GUIDES elsewhere directs the same deletion once decided: A.3 "the correct outcome is to remove it from tools with a recorded reason" and Phase 3 "remove it from tools with the reason recorded." Both docs contemplate removal; GUIDES sequences it (recorded decision, separate commit) and SENTENCING says nothing that conflicts with that sequencing.

5. Both docs are trivially followable together: the decision-maker answers GUIDES OQ1 (with two concurring recommendations in hand), records it in DECISIONS.md per GUIDES Phase 3, and then removes or narrows the tools row in its own commit, which simultaneously satisfies SENTENCING B.4's conditional and resolves SENTENCING OQ9. No directive in either document is violated by that path.

The only residual kernel is that the same-day docs do not cross-reference each other and SENTENCING's Section 0 uses the word "Verdict" for what its own body labels a recommendation. That is a presentational/coordination nit, not the "cannot both be followed," verdict-impacting contradiction the finding alleges. The finding is refuted: it misreads a conditional recommendation as an unconditional executed decision, misstates SENTENCING's open questions, and treats a commit-timing rule as a disposition conflict when both docs recommend the same disposition.

### SENTENCING-BOND-CONCEPT.md

**Alleged:** W5 records ... `Florida criminal punishment code scoresheet` at 70 per month at state level.

**Why refuted:** The finding's core evidence is factually wrong. It asserts "No 70/month figure for that query exists anywhere in the repository" and that the only 70/month in the repo belongs to 'identity theft Florida statute'. Both are false: docs/research/briefs/TOOLS.md lines 90-91 record verbatim that "`Florida criminal punishment code scoresheet` returns 70/month at Florida state level" (Phase C brief, research date 2026-08-13, the session in which sibling briefs mark volume pulls "verified 2026-08-13"), and 70/month figures also exist for 18 usc 371, 18 usc 1343, 18 usc 2252, and sex-crimes queries. TOOLS.md is explicitly listed among the concept doc's inputs (SENTENCING-BOND-CONCEPT.md line 10), so the statistic is supported, not fabricated. The only surviving kernel is a citation-label slip: A.3 says "W5 records" the figure, and W5 proper (tools-and-hooks.md) indeed contains no absolute volumes (its method note says none were extractable); the figure comes from TOOLS.md, the Phase C brief that extends W5's workstream. That is a one-word attribution imprecision within a sentence whose other two facts the finding itself concedes are genuinely in W5 — not the "unsupported volume statistic" alleged. Because the substantive claim was correct and the finding materially mischaracterizes the source base, the finding is refuted; if the residual citation nit is counted at all, it is low severity.

## Unverified findings (below the verification cap; not corrected, not dismissed)

The four medium findings are all cross-document design conflicts from the
consistency agent, not factual errors. They belong to the Phase 0
gate-architecture decision (see D28) rather than to a correction pass.

- **[medium]** (consistency) SEAL-EXPUNGE-CONCEPT.md (vs GUIDES-CONCEPT.md) E.3 vs GUIDES F.3 G5: SEAL E.3: 'One deliberate reversal. check-rendered.mts exits 0 with a notice when .next is absent. For this gate a missing artifact must FAIL, because "the tool page is not there" and "the tool page contains none of its traps" produce the same green run otherwise.' GUIDES G5 prescribes the opposite for the same postbuild stage: 'Keep the existing skip-with-notice behaviour when .next is absent, but only after G1 has asserted the route exists.'
  - Evidence offered: Two docs prescribe incompatible missing-artifact policy for the same postbuild harness, each justified by the identical rationale sentence ('X is not built' and 'X contains none of its provisions/traps' produce the same green run). GUIDES' condition is also unsatisfiable as written: G1 is itself a postbuild check that works by enumerating .next/server/app/resources/guides/\*.html (GUIDES F.3 G1), so when .next is absent G1 cannot have asserted anything and the skip is exactly the silent green SEAL's reversal exists to prevent. Verified against scripts/check-rendered.mts lines 39-43, which does console.log a notice and process.exit(0) when .next/server/app is missing. A single npm postbuild pipeline cannot both fail and exit 0 in the same state; no doc reconciles the two rules.
- **[medium]** (consistency) GUIDES-CONCEPT.md (vs SEAL-EXPUNGE-CONCEPT.md and SENTENCING-BOND-CONCEPT.md) D.2 / F.3 vs SEAL E.2-E.3 vs SENTENCING F.2: GUIDES D.2 presents measuredPages as 'one measured-surface registry' that the five gates iterate 'rather than charges', calling it 'the load-bearing implementation decision'; but the registry it defines contains only charges and guides ('[...charges.map(...), ...guides.map(...)]'), while the other two docs wire their pages into the same gates through two further, different mechanisms that the registry does not subsume.
  - Evidence offered: Three uncoordinated designs for one hole. SEAL E.2 extends 'pageCopy with a tool-copy extractor' plus a new standalone gate 'check:tool-rendered' (E.3); SENTENCING F.2 instead gives 'tools a copy surface in site.ts analogous to pageCopy' inside a new three-layer gate named 'check:tools' with a headless DOM render (Layer 3) that neither other doc has; GUIDES D.2/F.3 route guides through measuredPages + guideCopy + a new 'check:provenance' and extensions G1/G5. ## Dispositions, 2026-08-20: the six rulings

Ruled by the client on this record. Application commit: see git history for
2026-08-20.

1. **Both guide verdicts re-derived from the corrected measurements.**
   GUIDES-CONCEPT Section 0 rewritten from the true counts rather than patched
   (guide 2: build, vacancy four stages wide; guide 1: re-scope to the release
   decision, resting on the measurement rather than the falsified inventory).
   Original Section 0 is in git history.
2. **One gate architecture: D29.** A single measured-surface registry holding
   every renderable page (charges, guides, tools), all gates iterating it; the
   three per-document mechanisms reconciled into that design.
3. **Missing artifact FAILs: D30.** SEAL E.3 adopted; GUIDES G5 rejected as
   unsatisfiable (its guard, G1, is itself postbuild). Resolves the first
   medium consistency finding.
4. **TOOLS.md bar not self-executing: D31.** Applying the not-recommended
   table to a planned asset requires a recorded decision. SENTENCING B.2
   reclassified as a recommendation. Resolves the third medium consistency
   finding.
5. **Bond estimator not built: D32.** Schedule folds into the after-an-arrest
   guide; cash versus surety comparison survives as its only interactive
   element; tools row removed in its own commit. Made as a fresh decision with
   the fourth medium finding's elision on the record (the research never said
   the guide absorbs the estimator; the plan had them coexisting). Resolves
